question: My app has one route for /users/me and another for /users/{user_id}, and requests to /users/me keep landing in the second one. What's going wrong?
gold_answer: Path operations are evaluated in order, so the fixed path /users/me must be declared before /users/{user_id}. Otherwise /users/{user_id} also matches /users/me and receives user_id with the value "me".

gold_chunk_sections.section: Path Parameters > Order matters

question: How do I make a route parameter swallow an entire file path with slashes in it, like home/johndoe/myfile.txt?
gold_answer: Use Starlette's path convertor and declare the route as /files/{file_path:path}, where the :path part tells it to match any path. If the value needs a leading slash, the URL needs a double slash, e.g. /files//home/johndoe/myfile.txt.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Path Parameters > Path parameters containing paths > Path convertor

question: Which values will FastAPI read as True when a query parameter is annotated as bool?
gold_answer: Values such as 1, true, True (any upper/lower case variation), on and yes are converted to True. Any other value is read as False.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Query Parameters > Query parameter type conversion

question: Which FastAPI release do I need before I can wrap a parameter type in Annotated?
gold_answer: Support for Annotated (and the recommendation to use it) was added in FastAPI 0.95.0. The docs say to upgrade to at least 0.95.1 before using it, because older versions raise errors.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Query Parameters and String Validations > Additional validation > Import `Query` and `Annotated`

question: How can I accept ?q=foo&q=bar and receive both values as a Python list?
gold_answer: Declare the parameter with a list type (for example list[str] | None) and use Query explicitly. Without Query, a list parameter would be interpreted as a request body.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Query Parameters and String Validations > Query parameter list / multiple values

question: I need a float that can be 0.5 but must never be exactly 0. Which validation argument should I use on Query or Path?
gold_answer: Use gt=0 (greater than) rather than ge. With gt=0, a value of 0.5 is valid but 0.0 or 0 are not; lt works the same way for upper bounds.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Path Parameters and Numeric Validations > Number validations: floats, greater than and less than

question: When one function takes an id from the URL, a Pydantic model and a plain int, how does FastAPI decide where each one comes from?
gold_answer: A parameter also declared in the path is a path parameter. A parameter of a singular type (int, float, str, bool, etc.) is read as a query parameter. A parameter typed as a Pydantic model is read from the request body.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Request Body > Request body + path + query parameters

question: Which HTTP status codes are not allowed to carry a response body?
gold_answer: Responses in the 100-199 range cannot have a body. 204 (No Content) must have no body, and 304 (Not Modified) must not have one either.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Response Status Code > About HTTP status codes

question: My Pydantic response model has defaults on several optional fields. How do I keep those out of the JSON when the values were never actually set?
gold_answer: Set response_model_exclude_unset=True in the path operation decorator so only explicitly set values are returned. response_model_exclude_defaults and response_model_exclude_none are also available, and values explicitly set to the same value as the default are still included.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Response Model - Return Type > Response Model encoding parameters > Use the `response_model_exclude_unset` parameter

question: How can I catch one of my own exception classes globally and turn it into a specific JSON error?
gold_answer: Register a handler with @app.exception_handler(YourException); it receives the Request and the exception and returns a response such as JSONResponse. In the docs example the custom exception ends up as an HTTP 418 with a JSON message.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Handling Errors > Install custom exception handlers

question: When I use a class as a dependency, how can I avoid typing the class name both as the annotation and inside Depends()?
gold_answer: Declare the class as the parameter's type and use Depends() with no argument; FastAPI then calls that class to create the instance. It is only a shortcut to reduce repetition.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Classes as Dependencies > Shortcut

question: Two of my dependencies share a sub-dependency and it only runs once per request. How do I make it run again every time it's needed?
gold_answer: Pass use_cache=False to Depends. By default FastAPI calls a repeated sub-dependency once per request and reuses the cached value.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Sub-dependencies > Using the same dependency multiple times

question: When does the cleanup code of a dependency with yield run by default, and how can I make it finish before the response is sent?
gold_answer: By default the exit code runs after the response is sent, because the default scope is "request". Using Depends(scope="function") makes it run after the path operation function returns but before the response is sent.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Dependencies with yield > Early exit and `scope`

question: What is the difference between BackgroundTask and BackgroundTasks, and which one should I import to use as a route parameter?
gold_answer: Import BackgroundTasks (with the s) from fastapi; it comes from starlette.background and can be declared as a path operation function parameter that FastAPI handles for you. Using BackgroundTask alone means creating it yourself and returning a Starlette Response that includes it.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Background Tasks > Technical Details

question: If I don't set allow_methods, allow_credentials or max_age on CORSMiddleware, what defaults apply?
gold_answer: allow_methods defaults to ['GET'], allow_credentials defaults to False, and max_age defaults to 600 seconds (allow_headers and expose_headers default to empty lists).

gold_chunk_sections.section: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) > Use `CORSMiddleware`

question: In a test with TestClient, how do I send form-encoded data instead of JSON, and how do I add request headers?
gold_answer: Use the data parameter for form data (the json parameter takes a Python object for a JSON body). Headers go in a dict passed as headers, and cookies in a dict passed as cookies.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Testing > Testing: extended example > Extended testing file

question: Why would I choose UploadFile over declaring an uploaded file parameter as bytes?
gold_answer: With bytes the whole file is held in memory, while UploadFile uses a spooled file that stays in memory up to a limit and then goes to disk, so it suits large files. It also gives metadata such as filename and content_type, an async file-like interface, and the underlying SpooledTemporaryFile.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Request Files > File Parameters with `UploadFile`

question: How do I serve Swagger UI at /documentation and switch ReDoc off?
gold_answer: Create the app with docs_url="/documentation" and redoc_url=None. Setting a URL parameter to None disables that docs interface.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Metadata and Docs URLs > Docs URLs

question: In the JWT tutorial code, what goes into the sub claim and what rules should it follow?
gold_answer: The sub key holds the identification of the token's subject, such as the username; using it is optional per the JWT spec. It should be a string that is unique across the whole application, and can be prefixed (e.g. username:) to avoid ID collisions.

gold_chunk_sections.section: OAuth2 with Password (and hashing), Bearer with JWT tokens > Update the `/token` *path operation* > Technical details about the JWT "subject" `sub`

question: Why does the SQLite engine in the SQLModel example get check_same_thread=False?
gold_answer: It lets FastAPI use the same SQLite database from different threads, which is needed because a single request can use more than one thread (for example in dependencies). A single session per request is still ensured through the session dependency.

gold_chunk_sections.section: SQL (Relational) Databases > Create the App with a Single Model > Create an Engine

question: What are the default minimum_size and compresslevel of the built-in gzip middleware?
gold_answer: minimum_size defaults to 500 bytes (smaller responses are not compressed) and compresslevel defaults to 9. It compresses responses for requests whose Accept-Encoding includes gzip.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Advanced Middleware > `GZipMiddleware`

question: How should I write my fastapi requirement so I pick up bug-fix releases automatically but not new minor versions?
gold_answer: Pin to a range such as fastapi>=0.112.0,<0.113.0. Below 1.0.0, MINOR versions can bring breaking changes, while PATCH versions are for bug fixes and non-breaking changes.

gold_chunk_sections.section: About FastAPI versions > Pin your `fastapi` version

question: Does fastapi run reload on code changes, and which address does it listen on?
gold_answer: No, auto-reload is disabled with fastapi run. It listens on 0.0.0.0, meaning all available IP addresses, which is how you would normally run in production such as in a container.

gold_chunk_sections.section: FastAPI CLI > `fastapi run`

question: What status code does RedirectResponse use if I don't pass one?
gold_answer: It uses 307 (Temporary Redirect) by default, including when it is set as response_class and the path operation returns just the URL. You can combine status_code with response_class to change it.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Custom Response - HTML, Stream, File, others > Available responses > `RedirectResponse`

question: A client of mine sends JSON without a Content-Type header and my endpoint stopped parsing the body. Is there a setting to get the old behavior back?
gold_answer: Yes, set strict_content_type=False on the app. Requests without a Content-Type header are then parsed as JSON, like in older versions; this setting was added in FastAPI 0.132.0.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Strict Content-Type Checking > Allowing Requests Without Content-Type

question: For the login endpoint in the password flow, what exact field names must the client send, and what keys must my JSON reply contain?
gold_answer: The client must send username and password as form data (not JSON), with an optional scope field. The reply must be a JSON object with access_token and token_type, where token_type is "bearer" for bearer tokens.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Simple OAuth2 with Password and Bearer > Get the `username` and `password`
Simple OAuth2 with Password and Bearer > Return the token

question: My container sits behind an Nginx that terminates TLS, and redirects point to http://localhost:8000/... instead of my public HTTPS address. What should I add to the container's start command and why?
gold_answer: Add --proxy-headers to the fastapi run command in the Dockerfile CMD (exec form), so the server trusts the headers the proxy sends about HTTPS and the original host. Without trusting them, a redirect such as /items to /items/ can point to http://localhost:8000/items/ instead of the public HTTPS URL.

gold_chunk_sections.section: FastAPI in Containers - Docker > Build a Docker Image for FastAPI > Dockerfile
Behind a Proxy > Proxy Forwarded Headers > Redirects with HTTPS

question: How can I load my app settings from a .env file and still swap them for different values in tests?
gold_answer: Set env_file in the Settings class's model_config to point at the dotenv file (python-dotenv is needed). Provide the settings through a dependency and, in tests, put a replacement function in app.dependency_overrides keyed by the original dependency, then reset the overrides to an empty dict afterwards.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Settings and Environment Variables > Reading a `.env` file > Read settings from `.env`
Testing Dependencies with Overrides > Overriding dependencies during testing > Use the `app.dependency_overrides` attribute

question: The code I put after the yield in my lifespan function never seems to run when my Docker container stops. What should I check in the Dockerfile?
gold_answer: Check that CMD uses the exec form (a JSON list of strings) rather than the shell form. The shell form prevents FastAPI from shutting down gracefully, so the lifespan shutdown code after the yield may not be triggered.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Lifespan Events > Lifespan
FastAPI in Containers - Docker > Build a Docker Image for FastAPI > Dockerfile

question: My middleware adds an X-Process-Time header, but JavaScript in the browser can't read it. What do I need to change?
gold_answer: Custom headers you want browser clients to see must be listed in the CORS configuration via the expose_headers parameter of CORSMiddleware. It defaults to an empty list, so nothing is exposed unless you add it.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Middleware > Create a middleware
CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) > Use `CORSMiddleware`

question: I want a route that normally returns 200 but returns 201 when it creates the item, and I still want the output filtered by my response model. How do I do that?
gold_answer: Declare a parameter of type Response in the path operation function and set status_code on that temporary response, then return your data as usual. FastAPI copies the status code into the final response, and the response_model still filters and converts what you return.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Response - Change Status Code > Use a `Response` parameter
Response Model - Return Type > `response_model` Parameter

question: What does OAuth2PasswordBearer do when the Authorization header is missing, and what status code and header should such an error carry?
gold_answer: OAuth2PasswordBearer responds directly with a 401 error if the Authorization header is missing or isn't 'Bearer ' plus a token. Per the spec a 401 should include WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, and since FastAPI 0.122.0 the built-in security classes return 401 instead of the older 403.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Security - First Steps > What it does

Use Old 403 Authentication Error Status Codes

question: Which FastAPI versions added Pydantic models for form fields, the option to forbid extra form fields, and Pydantic models for query parameters?
gold_answer: Form models are supported since FastAPI 0.113.0, forbidding extra form fields since 0.114.0, and Pydantic models for query parameters since 0.115.0.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Form Models

question: I mounted static files at /static. How do I link the stylesheet from a Jinja2 template, and what is the name argument on the mount for?
gold_answer: In the template call url_for('static', path='/styles.css'), which works because the StaticFiles mount was given name="static". That name is what FastAPI uses internally to refer to the mounted app.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Static Files > Details
Templates > Templates and static files

question: If my Pydantic header model has a field called save_data, which HTTP header does it expect, and how do I keep the underscore?
gold_answer: Underscores in header parameter names are converted to hyphens by default, so save_data expects the save-data header. To keep underscores set convert_underscores=False on Header, keeping in mind some proxies and servers reject headers with underscores.

question: How do I let a query parameter be None?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (not required): give it a default of None, e.g. q: str | None = None, so the client may omit it. Reading 2 (required but nullable): declare None as an allowed type but give no default, which forces clients to send a value even if it is None.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Query Parameters > Optional parameters
Query Parameters and String Validations > Required parameters > Required, can be `None`

question: How do I run some code when my app starts up?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (recommended): use the lifespan parameter with an async context manager, where code before the yield runs at startup and code after it at shutdown. Reading 2 (deprecated): register startup event handlers, but if a lifespan is provided the startup and shutdown handlers are no longer called, so it is one or the other.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Lifespan Events > Lifespan
Lifespan Events > Alternative Events (deprecated) > `startup` event

question: How do I return a different status code than the default?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (fixed per route): pass status_code to the path operation decorator, as an int or a fastapi.status constant. Reading 2 (chosen at runtime, keeping response_model): declare a Response parameter and set its status_code. Reading 3 (extra status codes): return a Response such as JSONResponse directly with the status you want, which skips model serialization and is not documented in OpenAPI.

gold_chunk_sections.section: Response Status Code
Response - Change Status Code > Use a `Response` parameter
Additional Status Codes > Additional status codes

question: How many server processes should I run for my FastAPI app?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (your own server or VM): start several workers with the --workers option of fastapi or uvicorn to use multiple CPU cores. Reading 2 (Kubernetes or another cluster): run a single Uvicorn process per container and handle replication at the cluster level instead of using workers.

gold_answer: Reading 1 (JSON Schema examples): pass examples on Body, Field or model_config's json_schema_extra, but Swagger UI does not show multiple JSON Schema examples. Reading 2 (multiple examples shown in the docs UI): use the OpenAPI-specific openapi_examples parameter, a dict of named examples each with summary, description and value.

question: How do I return an HTML page from a FastAPI route?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (raw HTML): set response_class=HTMLResponse and return the HTML string (or return an HTMLResponse directly), which sets Content-Type to text/html. Reading 2 (rendered templates): install jinja2, create Jinja2Templates and return templates.TemplateResponse with the template name, the request and a context dict.

question: How do I make every endpoint require the same dependency?
gold_answer: Reading 1 (the whole application): pass dependencies=[Depends(...)] when creating the FastAPI app, and they apply to all path operations. Reading 2 (a group of endpoints): put dependencies on an APIRouter, which applies to all path operations in that router and runs before decorator and parameter dependencies.
